title: Route Redistribution: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Two parts of your network run different routing protocols. They can't understand each other's routes. Redistribution is the translator.

scenes.heading: The bilingual translator
scenes.narration: A translator carries routes from one language into the other. You set it up under the protocol that receives the routes. E I G R P needs a seed metric, or nothing arrives. O S P F gives redistributed routes a default metric of twenty. And O S P F needs the subnets keyword for subnetted routes.

scenes.heading: Examples
scenes.narration: Two quick examples. Into O S P F, redistribute with subnets. Add the subnets keyword. Into E I G R P, give a metric. The metric is required.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. O S P F's default seed metric is twenty. E I G R P has no default seed metric. Without subnets, only classful networks come across.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Redistribution moves routes between protocols. E I G R P needs a seed metric. O S P F needs the subnets keyword. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva redistribution lab.
